And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said to him, "Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you."
And he himself said to them, "What do you want from me, that I should do it for you?"
And they said to him, "Grant us that we may sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, on that day of your glory."
And Jesus said to them, "You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to receive the baptism with which I am baptized, to be baptized
with it?" And they said to him, "We are able." Jesus answered and said to them, "The cup that I drink you will indeed drink, and the baptism with which I was baptized you will be baptized with.

And the Sadducees came to him, who say that there is no resurrection, and they questioned him
and said to him, "Teacher, Moses wrote this for us: that if someone's brother dies, and he has a wife and leaves no child, his brother should take his wife and raise up an heir for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first took a wife and died, and left no
child. And the second took her, and he died and left no child. And the third
likewise, up to the seventh, and they left no child. Last of all, the woman also died.
Now in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be of them? For all seven had her as wife."
Jesus answered them and said, "Is this not why you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?
When they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like angels in heaven.
And as for the dead rising, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him: 'I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob'?
He is not the God of the dead but of the living. You are greatly mistaken."
And one of the scribes came up; he had heard them as they were disputing with him, and he knew that he had answered them well.

Jesus stood opposite the treasury and watched how the people were putting copper coins into the treasury; and many rich people put in a great deal.
And a poor widow came and put in two
small coins. And he called his disciples and said to them, "Amen, I say to you, this poor widow has put more into the treasury
than all of them. For they all gave out of their abundance, but she out of her poverty gave everything she had, her whole living."
And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him, "Teacher, look what stones these are and what buildings!"
Jesus answered and said to them: Do you see these great buildings? Amen, I say to you, not one stone will be left upon another.
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately:
Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the signs when these things are about to be fulfilled?
Jesus answered and said to them: Take care that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name and will say, 'I am he,' and they will lead many astray.

And immediately, as soon as it was dawn, the chief priests took counsel with the elders and the scribes and the whole council, and they bound Jesus and led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Pilate asked him and said, "Are you the king of the Jews?" But Jesus answered and said to him, "You say it."
And the chief priests accused him of many things, and he
answered nothing. But Pilate asked him again and said, "Do you answer nothing? Look how many things they testify against you."

And they went into the tomb and saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white garment, and they were alarmed.
But he said to them, "Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Look, here is the place where
